To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the vasodepressor effects of centrally administered phenylephehine are mediated by a-adrenergie receptors in supramedular brain areas (possibly hypothalamus), that the magnitude of the vasodepressor effect is significantly greater in SHR than in normotensives and DOCA-salt hyper- tensive rats, and that the vasodepression is probably due to a reduced brain norepinephrme concentration that increases the number of a-adrenerglc receptors available.
central a-adrenergically mediated depressor responses to intracarotoid injections of phenylephine were greater in SHR than in normotensives or DOCA-salts.

central alpha-adrenergic vasodepressor mechanisms were more active in spontaneously hypertensive (SHR) rats than in normotensives or DOCA-hypertensive rats, and that the increased activity was due to decreased levels of endogenous noradrenaline in the brain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the central nervous system (CNS) control of blood pressure and its role in the pathogenesis of hypertension.
the role of central a-adrenergie mechanisms in blood pressure regulation.
a study of central mechanisms for cardiovascular control.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
central adrenergic mechanisms of cardiovascular regulation are altered in SHR.
central a-adrenergically mediated hypotensive mechanisms are augmented in spontaneously hypertensive animals.
the a-adrenergically induced vasodepression in SHR may be due to the increased availability of the a-adrenergeic receptors in the brain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
central adrenergic mechanisms play an important role in the pathogenesis of hypertension.

the central nervous system is a major site of blood pressure control and that the central a-adrenergically induced vasodepressive system is augmented in SHR, which may be one of the factors contributing to the maintenance of high blood pressure in these rats.
the central nervous system is a very important regulator of blood pressure and that this regulation is altered in the hypertensive state.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a-adrenergically mediated vasodepression in the brain can be augmented in SHR.
a-adrenergie vasodepressor responses in the central nervous system are augmented in SHR.
the central adrenergic system plays a role in blood pressure regulation, and this system may contribute to the pathogenesis of essential hypertension.
